title: Find out what stopped the probe in SwiftUI's focus update on 2026-11-22, and whether a person could hit it
goal: The loop's probe app stopped once at 03:12 on 2026-11-22, inside SwiftUI's own start-up loop while it was updating keyboard focus for accessibility, passing through the menu bar menu. It happened once, while a runner was trying out an unfinished change. Find out whether the shipped app can still do this, and if it can, fix it.

log.note: Triage 2026-11-22: moved p1 to p2 and retitled as a question. The notes carry no command that shows the crash, so it cannot be re-run. What I read in the report: a SwiftUI precondition (assertionFailure < precondition < runApp's UpdateGroup.dispatchImmediately) under AccessibilityNode.updateFocus > ViewRendererHost.focusResponder > MultiViewResponder.visit > MenuBarMenu's body. HeldDragKeys.swift:111 (photonz_nextEvent) is only on the stack because it runs the event loop. The probe launched 03:08:16 and stopped 03:12:26, during long-edit pass 27, whose runner was working on the timeline lanes and reading the cost of SwiftUI's accessibility focus walk. So the probe was most likely built from pass 27's unfinished tree (binary uuid 3c46339e, not today's dist probe). Same family as a-crash-in-a-runner-s-own-half-built-probe-is-lo. One report with this signature, none since. Different from the-app-crashed-in-nsapplication-photonz-nexteve (that was a window-size runaway, fixed in c23a205be).

Acceptance as a question: (1) run the walks pass 27 ran (painted-clips-take-a-hand-walk, speed-walk, the timeline walks) a few times on today's probe and say whether this report comes back; (2) if it does not, close as caused by an unfinished build and log that on a-crash-in-a-runner-s-own-half-built-probe-is-lo; if it does, fix it with a walk that fails first.

Read the crash against pass 27's session transcript (bc978243): the probe launched 03:08:16 by /tmp/pz27-nodes-run.sh, which attached lldb to it with three breakpoints in SwiftUI's accessibility focus walk and a Python callback that ran EvaluateExpression(object_getClassName) on the main thread at every visit; perl's 250 s alarm killed lldb (log: 'Alarm clock: 14', walk exit 4) at 03:12:3x, the crash is stamped 03:12:26. The stack shows MultiViewResponder.visit 'calling' Photonz_main and then App.main > runApp > precondition: that is lldb's injected-call return address (the executable's entry point) being run for real once the debugger died mid-expression, so SwiftUI's runApp ran a second time and trapped (ESR brk 1). Theory: debugger artefact, not app code. Now checking it on the shipped probe.

Reproduction on today's probe (main 122e997ad, built by the first speed-walk run, Grants: Screen Recording granted, screen unlocked): (a) the exact walk the probe was running when it died, /tmp/pz27-ax-walk.json recreated (6 min reference edit, 20 s of play, speed edits nothing/pick/unpick/pick), 3 runs, exit 0 each; (b) Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/speed-walk.json, 3 runs, exit 0 each; (c) Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build painted-clips-take-a-hand painted-gap a-transition-is-picked-at-the-cut a-click-on-a-clip-piece several-picked-clips-change-track a-long-edit-has-one-zoom-lane reference-edit-opens an-editing-session scrub-never-blacks-out the-panel-catches-up a-cut-slid-under-a-still-pointer every-handle-lights-on-hover clip-bar (pass 27's own list, 12 walks), 3 rounds, '12 passed, 0 failed' each, 0 CRASHED. No new Photonz report in ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports (newest is still the 03:12 one), and grep for 'closure #1 in closure #1 in runApp' or 'AccessibilityNode.updateFocus' across every .ips there finds only this one report.

Correction to triage: the probe was NOT built from an unfinished tree. Pass 27's transcript shows its first source edit (TimelineTrackRows.swift) at 03:16:51, after the crash. What it was doing at 03:08 to 03:12 was /tmp/pz27-nodes-run.sh: lldb attached to the probe with breakpoints in ViewRendererHost.focusResponder and ResponderNode.visitFocusResponders, a Python callback running frame.EvaluateExpression(object_getClassName) on the main thread, and perl 'alarm 250' killing lldb (its output: 'Alarm clock: 14', walk exit 4). lldb's injected call returns to the executable's entry point, which is why the stack has Photonz_main/$main sitting ABOVE MultiViewResponder.visit and then App.main > runApp > precondition: the debugger died mid-expression and the thread ran the app's main a second time. A person cannot get there. Logged the finding on a-crash-in-a-runner-s-own-half-built-probe-is-lo, whose dirty-tree stamp would not have caught this one.
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Not an app bug and a person cannot hit it. The 03:12 probe crash was pass 27's lldb experiment: the debugger was attached with Python callbacks evaluating expressions in SwiftUI's focus walk and was killed mid-expression by a 250 s alarm, so the thread returned into the app's entry point and SwiftUI's runApp ran a second time (that is why Photonz_main sits mid-stack). The probe was built from committed code (first edit came at 03:16). On today's probe (main 122e997ad) the exact walk it was running, speed-walk and pass 27's 12 timeline walks each ran 3 times: all green, 0 CRASHED, no new crash report. Finding logged on a-crash-in-a-runner-s-own-half-built-probe-is-lo with a new checklist item for debugger-attached probes.
